rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.10 describe a two-factor pot experiment (drip vs flood irrigation x 18/24/30 C soil temperature, four replicates) with the authors' own measurements of photosynthesis, enzymes, hormones, pollen viability and yield. Q2: Table 1 and Section 3.1 show leaf Pn, Gs, Ci and Tr lower in DI than FI (Pn 14.4 vs 16.3 at 30 C; main effect 15% lower); Discussion states that at 30 C DI reduced photosynthetic performance relative to FI; Section 3.2-3.5 and Table 3 show DI-FI differences in MDA, proline, hormones, pollen viability and yield were largest at 18 C, and Abstract/Conclusion state low soil temperature had a greater negative effect under DI than FI. Q4: the study measures the intermediate stress and reproductive variables through which the yield loss arises - antioxidant enzymes, MDA and proline (Figs 2-3), spikelet hormones (Fig 4), pollen viability (Fig 5), surviving branches/spikelets (Table 2) and seed setting rate (Table 3). Q7: Conclusion states that at 30 C the recommended 90-95% field capacity is already a mild stress environment for cv. T-43 and that drip irrigation with cold water aggravates this stress, which could be avoided by warming water in storage ponds before application, i.e. low irrigation/soil water temperature is the stated condition for the exacerbated harm. Q9: Figs 2-5 report error bars as SE (n = 3) for enzyme activities, MDA/proline, hormone concentrations and pollen viability.
rows.notes: Q3: all results come from a single pot experiment; different variables (gas exchange, enzyme assays, hormones, yield counts) are different measurements within one experimental method rather than independent methods establishing the same result, so rated no. Q5/Q6: one sandy-loam soil, one cultivar (T-43), pots in a laboratory; no sites or field scale. Q7 rated yes with some doubt, since low temperature was the experimental factor and the effect could be read as an interaction; the Conclusion nonetheless frames cold water as the condition and warming water as the remedy. Q8: no explicit limitations stated (pot scale, 10-day temperature treatment, single cultivar not discussed as restrictions). Q9: Tables 1 (photosynthesis) and 3 (yield) give only letter groupings and F values without SE; dispersion is reported only for the figure variables.

notes: Full text appears complete. Note the abstract states that drip irrigation reduced photosynthetic activity at 30 C, but Table 1 shows DI below FI at all temperatures with no significant T x I interaction for photosynthesis; the review passage's framing follows the authors' abstract.
